title: Type State Pattern
concept: The Type State pattern encodes object state in the type system — making invalid operations impossible at compile time rather than catching them at runtime.
why: Runtime state checks fail when you forget. Type State moves state into types — the compiler prevents you from calling .send() on a closed connection.
tips: Type State eliminates entire categories of runtime errors — invalid states are unrepresentable
Use phantom type parameters — they exist only at compile time, zero runtime cost
Document state transitions in a comment or diagram — complex state machines need visual docs
Combine Type State with invariants for ultimate safety: type ensures valid operations, invariant ensures valid data
common_mistakes: Making state transitions consuming when they should be borrowing — prevents chaining operations
Too many state types — creates excessive generic noise and reduced readability
Not using PhantomData for zero-size state markers — wastes memory at runtime
